newsitem.title: UK: BAT seeks $3 bln tobacco fighting fund in US - paper.
newsitem.headline: BAT seeks $3 bln tobacco fighting fund in US - paper.

text.p: British-based tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T. Industries is trying to set up a $3 billion fund from across the U.S. tobacco industry to cushion the rising costs there of legal claims against cigarette companies, The Sunday Telegraph reported.

The report follows news last week that U.S. company Liggett, the maker of Chesterfield cigarettes, became the first tobacco company to admit smoking is addictive and could cause cancer. It made the announcement when settling 22 cases of health compensation claims made by smokers.

The Sunday Telegraph said B.A.T., through its U.S. subsidiary Brown and Williamson, aims to convince US tobacco industry chiefs of the need for a fund which would act as insurance against legal claims while covering the cost of fighting court cases.
B.A.T. has contacted Philip Morris, RJ Reynolds and Lorillard about the joint approach, the paper said.
